newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: UK FIRM OUTBIDS ILLOVO FOR IVORIAN SUGAR.
newsitem.headline: UK FIRM OUTBIDS ILLOVO FOR IVORIAN SUGAR.

text.p: British commodity group ED & F Man Group Plc looks to have pipped Illovo Sugar Ltd to the post for a slice of Ivory Coast sugar firm, SODESUCRE, which is being privatised.

The public opening of bids by the privatisation committee, held in open session to ensure transparency, showed ED&F Man had entered the highest bid. An official said final results were likely "within 10 days".
SODESUCRE, which produces and sells sugar and is 100 percent owned by the state, is being split into two lots, each comprising two production plants plus their plantations.

Companies were invited to bid for a 55 percent stake in each lot. The state will retain 20 percent, employees will take five percent and the balance of 20 percent will be floated on the Abidjan stock exchange.
The biggest bid for Lot A, comprising two sites in the northwest of the country near Ferkessedougo, came from a group comprising ED & F Man and Britain's Commonwealth Development Corporation.
It valued the lot at 14.6 billion CFA francs ($25 million). After a deduction for debt, the consortium put in a bid of 6.4 billion for a 55 percent stake.
An Illovo spokesman said the South African company had entered bids for both lots, stating a preference for Lot A.
Lot B comprised one plant in Borotou in the northwest, plus one in Zuenoula in the centre.

The committee received two practically identical bids for this lot. SIFCA, a private Ivorian company, valued it at 27 billion CFA francs and said that, after debt, that translated into an offer of 13.789 billion CFA francs for a 55 percent stake.

A Senegalese company, Cie Sucriere Senegalaise, also valued the lot at 27 billion CFA francs, but its offer for the 55 percent stake came in at a tiny, but possibly significant, 500,000 CFA francs less.

The final decision of the committee will take into account any conditions attached to bids. Most of the bids read out appeared to commit bidders to take on all or most of the staff currently employed by SODESUCRE. ($ = 585 CFA francs)
